nav.desktopOnly: This section is available in the desktop app.

page.title: Settings
page.subtitle: Everything here configures the bundled OpenCode runtime — one config, no copies.

runtime.title: Agent runtime
runtime.hint: opencode serve, driven over its HTTP + SSE API
runtime.proxyNoneDetected: No system proxy detected — connections go direct.
runtime.mirrorHint: Optional mirrors, used only when setting up Python tools (Jupyter, science databases) on networks where pypi.org / github.com are slow. Leave blank for defaults.

acp.title: Agent
acp.hint: Which agent this app drives: the bundled OpenCode runtime, or any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) over stdio.
acp.bundledHint: The default runtime — providers, skills, plan mode and saved conversations.
acp.limits: An ACP agent runs as a command on this computer, in the current workspace folder. It owns its own model, skills and history, so the model picker, plan mode and saved conversations stay with OpenCode — sessions started on an ACP agent are listed only while the app is running.

updates.title: App updates
updates.hint: Checks GitHub Releases at most once every 24 hours
updates.autoCheckHint: Enabled by default. The app checks at most once per day.
updates.showBadgeHint: Show a red dot on Settings when a newer release is found.
updates.privacy: Only the public GitHub Releases API is contacted. No workspace files or API keys are sent.

model.title: Model
model.hint: Providers below supply the models you can pick here
model.connectPrompt: Connect the runtime to configure models.
model.notSet: Not set — pick a default model
model.searchPlaceholder: Search by model, ID, or provider
model.retiredDefault: Retired by its provider: {{model}} is no longer served and every turn will fail. Pick another model below.
model.catalogUnavailable: The model catalog is currently unavailable.

providers.title: Providers
providers.hint: Authentication, custom endpoints, and imported OpenCode logins
providers.webHint: Connected providers — read-only from the browser
providers.webNote: API keys and custom endpoints are set on the machine running the workbench — in the desktop app, or with `osd auth set` when it runs headless. Credentials never cross the gateway.
providers.connectPrompt: Connect the runtime to manage providers.
providers.searchPlaceholder: Connect a provider — search {{count}} (anthropic, openrouter, deepseek…)
providers.waitingForBrowser: Waiting for you to finish in the browser…
providers.pasteCode: Paste the code from the browser
providers.customNamePlaceholder: Name — e.g. Ollama, My DeepSeek gateway
providers.customKeyPlaceholder: API key — optional, Ollama needs none
providers.noModelsFound: No models reported by the endpoint.
providers.importLogin: Already use the OpenCode CLI? Import its login

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.hint: Extra tools for the agent (Model Context Protocol) — e.g. a Jupyter or browser MCP
mcp.connectPrompt: Connect the runtime to configure MCP servers.
mcp.jupyterDescription: lets the agent drive real notebooks · isolated env w/ numpy·pandas·matplotlib, ~500 MB on first run · once set up, the app's Run button uses it too, so you and the agent share one Python

browser.label: Browser control
browser.title: Browser
browser.hint: Let the agent drive a real browser — navigate, click, fill forms, and read pages.
browser.description: Let the agent open pages, click, fill forms, and read the web — reusing your Chrome login.
browser.noChromeWillDownload: No Chrome detected — a private browser will be downloaded on first use.
browser.privateNote: Uses a separate downloaded browser that never touches your Chrome. Starts logged out; downloaded automatically on first use.
browser.reuseNote: Reuses a copy of “{{name}}”. The agent acts as that logged-in account; your real Chrome profile is never modified. Navigation still follows your approval mode.
browser.isolatedNote: Isolated profile — the agent starts logged out. Pick an account above to reuse its logins.
browser.downloaded: Browser downloaded — you can enable browser control now.
browser.capCore: Standard — navigate, click, read, screenshot, run JS
browser.allowedDomainsHint: One per line. Empty means no restriction. Supports patterns like *.example.com.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.hint: Local-first — projects live in projects/ and standalone sessions in sessions/

review.title: Review
review.hint: A read-only reviewer agent that audits finished work for traceability, statistics, units and provenance.
review.autoTitle: Review after every turn that changes files
review.autoHint: Runs one extra model turn in the background per change. The conversation stays usable; read-only turns are skipped.

python.title: Local Python kernel
python.hint: Runs notebook cells in the app. Uses your Jupyter environment when set up (same Python as the agent), else auto-detects — or set an explicit interpreter below

toast.interpreterSet: Interpreter set — notebook cells now run on it.
toast.folderSet: New sessions will be created in this folder.
toast.defaultModelReset: Default model {{old}} is no longer available — switched to {{model}}
toast.configRebuilt: The agent runtime's settings file could not be read, so it was moved to {{path}} and rebuilt. Providers and MCP servers may need adding again.
toast.couldNotFetchModels: Could not fetch models from the endpoint
toast.endpointFieldsRequired: Name, base URL and at least one model id are required.
toast.endpointAdded: {{name}} added — its models are now selectable above.
toast.couldNotAddMcp: Could not add the MCP server
toast.couldNotRemoveMcp: Could not remove the MCP server
toast.noOpenCodeLoginFound: No OpenCode CLI login found on this machine.
toast.couldNotSetProxy: Could not apply the proxy setting

dataFlow.title: Privacy & data flow
dataFlow.subtitle: What stays on this machine, and exactly what leaves it.

local.heading: Stays on this machine
local.workspaceFiles: Your workspace files and raw data
local.codeExecution: Code execution — the Python kernel and Jupyter run locally; datasets are processed here, never uploaded in bulk.
local.sessionHistory: Session history and provenance records, in the app's private data folder.
local.providerKeys: Provider keys and login tokens — an app-private file readable only by your account; never written to the workspace, provenance, logs, or exports.

remote.heading: Sent to your model provider
remote.messages: Your messages, and the file contents / command output the agent reads to do the task you asked for.
remote.notBackground: Nothing is sent in the background — data leaves only during a conversation turn.
remote.providerPolicy: What the provider retains is governed by its own data policy.

dataFlow.skillsHint: Skills and MCP servers you add may make their own network calls — review them before installing.

modal.title: Cloud compute (Modal)
modal.subtitle: Run GPU / elastic jobs on Modal with your own account — then just ask the agent.

readyHint.prefix: Ask the agent to run heavy work on Modal — it uses the

remoteCompute.title: Remote compute
remoteCompute.subtitle: Run jobs on your own servers over SSH — CPU or GPU; Slurm optional. Uses your own SSH keys; nothing is installed on the machine.
remoteCompute.empty: No machines yet — add one below.
remoteCompute.signInRequired: sign-in required — this machine asks for a password or a code
remoteCompute.signOutTitle: Close the shared connection to this machine
remoteCompute.sharingUnavailable: needs a password or code, which requires OpenSSH connection sharing (unavailable on Windows)

remote.title: Remote Access
remote.hint: Turn this desktop into a secure API — reach your sessions and files from a phone or another computer on your network, a CLI, or a tunnel. Off by default.
remote.enableHint: Start the authenticated gateway. Bound to this device only until you allow the local network below.
remote.loopbackUrlHint: Open in a browser on this Mac, or point a CLI here.
remote.bindingHint: Where the gateway listens. Only enable the local network on a network you trust.
remote.lanWarn: This exposes the gateway to everyone on your local network. Anyone with the token can drive the agent and read your workspace files. Only do this on a network you trust. Continue?
remote.lanActive: Reachable by other devices on your network. Keep the token secret.
remote.modeFullHint: Clients can create sessions, send prompts, run tools, and answer approvals.
remote.modeReadonlyHint: Clients can read sessions and files only — no prompts, tools, or approvals.
remote.tokenHint: Clients authenticate with this bearer token.
remote.regenerated: New token generated — existing clients must reconnect.
remote.openHint: The copied link includes the token — open it on another device to connect, no typing needed.
remote.connectPrompt: Enter the access token from the desktop app → Settings → Remote Access.
remote.acpHint: Drive this workspace from Zed, JetBrains, Neovim or any editor that speaks the Agent Client Protocol. Paste this agent entry into the editor's settings; it connects over the gateway above, with the access the token allows.
remote.acpNodeHint: The editor launches this script with Node 18+. The token is passed in the environment, not on the command line.

cli.title: Terminal command (osd)
cli.hint: The workbench from a terminal — sessions, projects, files, and a headless server for a machine with no screen. Installed with the app; no setup.
cli.readyPath: Ready — run `osd` in a new terminal.
cli.readyProfile: Ready — added to {{profile}}. Run `osd` in a new terminal.
cli.readyEnvironment: Ready — added to your user PATH. Run `osd` in a new terminal.
cli.unreachable: Installed, but nothing on your PATH reaches it. Add this line to your shell profile:
cli.notInstalled: Not installed. Use the button, or restart the app.
cli.unavailable: This build does not carry the osd command.
cli.occupied: A file this app did not write already has that name — rename it first.

memory.title: Memory
memory.hint: Lasting context the agent reads before every conversation, so you stop re-explaining a project.
memory.enableHint: Off means neither layer is loaded — useful for a throwaway question. Your files are kept either way.
memory.globalHint: Applies to every project: who you are, your tools, how you want answers written.
memory.globalPlaceholder:
# About me
- I work on …
- Prefer SI units and cite sources.
memory.projectHint: Applies only to conversations in this project: goals, terminology, data paths, decisions.
memory.projectNoneHint: Each project keeps its own memory file.
memory.projectNoneBody: Open a project to edit its memory.
memory.disabledNote: Memory is switched off, so this file is not loaded right now.

agentModels.title: Model and effort per agent
agentModels.hint: Run a reviewer or explorer on a fast model while the main agent reasons on a strong one, and pin how hard each one thinks.
agentModels.noModels: Connect a provider to choose models.
agentModels.primaryHint: build and plan run the messages you send. A model set here applies unless you pick one inside a conversation, which wins for that conversation only.

ssh.title: Sign in to {{host}}
ssh.hint: This machine authenticates interactively. Sign in once and every later command — yours and the agent's — reuses the same connection.
ssh.privacy: Sent only to ssh on this machine. Never stored, logged, or written to provenance.
